reviews.text: [i]Striving for Light[/i] is an action roguelike with hack-and-slash combat and an infinitely expanding skill tree. It’s a novel idea for a roguelike but given the game’s Early Access status, there’s a lot of room to grow. [h2]Graphics[/h2] The handpainted art style is rough around the edges but has an indie charm. Everything looks a little odd or goofy, but not outright bad. Sometimes the motion blur is a bit much, but my only major complaint is the lack of visibility caused by certain skill upgrades. You can add fire and explosions to your attacks, but when you combine it with the AoE size increase, you get massive orange circles covering half the screen. [h2]Gameplay – Combat[/h2] You begin each run with a ranged and melee weapon that you can switch between during combat. There’s a stamina system, but it isn’t shared between ranged and melee, so your basic strategy will involve using up all of your mana on ranged attacks, then switching to melee to use endurance while your mana recharges, continuing this loop as need be. It’s not the most complex system ever designed, but it adds a tactical flair to the combat, at least early on. Later, as you acquire more upgrades and focus on a certain playstyle, you’ll probably have enough mana/endurance to only use one attack type, unless you go for a jack-of-all-trades build. In typical roguelike fashion, your goal is to clear floors of enemies while collecting items and upgrades. Each floor has a boss fight, but it’s only an upgraded version of a standard enemy instead of a unique monster. There are a handful of different floor types, but the only noticeable differences are the color palette and the environmental hazards. Once you make it far enough, even these minor changes go away. Every floor is full of each hazard type, crammed into a big pile. They become your biggest threat because they are the only enemy you can’t kill. [h2]Gameplay – Progression[/h2] Instead of a standard skill tree, your potential upgrades will be laid out in a randomized web for you to choose from, generating new branches as you level up. This means min-maxing your character won’t be much of an option, as you’ll be forced to occasionally take an upgrade you don’t want, simply because you have no good choices left. If [i]Striving for Light[/i] was an ARPG, I would find it annoying, but the randomness works well for a roguelike trying to encourage the player to use different skill builds on each run. Unfortunately, while I like the overall concept, the skill web is mostly comprised of simple stat bonuses. There are a handful of more impactful skills, but they are distributed sparingly across the web. The result is that your character gets better in terms of basic stats like damage and speed, but your tactics don’t change much. Build options are quite limited, with only ranged attacks and melee attacks being viable options. Technically, you can go for a companion-based build, but their poor AI coupled with their low damage output means that they are always inferior to upgrading your own stats. Going for a standard skill build also results in quickly becoming far too powerful. It got to the point where I could kill every enemy on the floor with a single attack (The developer seems to have made a change to fix this post-release, so it may not be relevant anymore). Similar to many modern roguelikes, there’s a meta-progression system where you can unlock weapons and skills that will show up next time you play. Yet even with everything unlocked, multiple runs feel the same. You only have a few possible builds and they aren’t that different from each other. Most of the weapons fail to stand out as a unique tool for a distinct playstyle. Everything just feels so “samey” that it kills any desire to play again, the cornerstone of any successful roguelike. [h2]Performance[/h2] Complaining about performance in an Early Access title isn’t entirely fair, but it's still important to note. It runs fine at first but clearly isn’t designed for long playthroughs. After your skill web gets large enough, it begins to lag badly, almost to the point of unusability. It also ran abysmally once I was deep into a run, but this was prior to a bug fix, so I can’t confirm that this issue remains. [h2]Verdict[/h2] I know it seems like I’m just hating on this indie game to be mean, but really I’m trying to give the developer honest feedback. I like the core framework and I think it has a lot of potential, but in its current state, it has too many flaws to recommend it. [h2]4/10[/h2] [quote] Moderate performance issues running on: [b]AMD Ryzen 9 5900X, 16 GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce 3070[/b] [/quote] [quote] [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36214917/]Follow our Curator Page for more in-depth reviews and recommendations[/url] [/quote]

Changed my opinion from positive to negative! The game gets regular updates and many new things are good but much more of them are not well implemented/executed which leads to a bad experience overall. The devs do try to listen to community feedback and a lot of the changes are as a result of it. But as i said: good intention/ideas but bad implementation of many of those . There's also too much eye-cancer when you get a good build going. You can barely see what is happening and where the enemies, their projectiles, or AoE fields are later on when your setup has tons of other stuff on the screen. The original skill tree is extremely badly executed overall and there's a lot of bug with the skill gems system. On top of that the respec/refund is only possible IF you get the specific consumable instead of unlimited like in the new legacy skill tree system. The legacy skill tree system is one of the worst things ever. It's extremely costly to level up considering how it costs more and more for every level but your light drops don\t get better with every level. On top of that it rewards much less stats compared to the original skill tree's equivalents (except for the max hp and energy being 1 in both places). There's a massive lack of damage nodes in the skill tree and eventually the game becomes a massive slog where it's not that hard to survive but it takes forever to kill things. There's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ kill streak system forced on us that is also executed in an even ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way (hitting mobs does not keep it going and you have to actually kill stuff unlike how many other games handle it). Kill streak systems are bad in the fist place but at least implement them properly. It would have been much better if mobs just gave more exp and the kill streak system is removed to equalize things. OR let me pick if i want it one way or the other if some people enjoy this disgusting killstreak system. There is also no way to reset a level and re-do it without having to progress to the next one. To finish a level you need to beat a "key" boss that makes it so you can progress further BUT now there's a new mechanic where each level has a 2nd boss which is awful. If that second boss appeared only every 5 or 10 stages it would make sense. Now those "big" bosses don't feel special. The general pacing and balance seems to have gotten worse. Now events (merchant boss, phoenix, hidden room boss, mob waves portal) seem to spawn into traps 99% of the time and you barely have any room to move around. Exiting the mob waves portal even for like a second stops the event and despawns the enemies. There shouldn't be an area in the first place or at least let us stay out of that area for 3-4 seconds.Ideally that area will cover the whole room it spawned into and just lock you inside that whole room (ofc no limited area = best). The merchant prevents you from exiting the circle and keeps you locked inside which si even stupider considering how small that circle is. Traps are extremely annoying and there's no way to destroy them and it would have been nice to let us destroy them.

下方旧测评是22年的，直到25年都能看见这个游戏经常在更新，我原以为这是个小游戏作者不会如此重视，毕竟评论数感觉销售额并没有涨。说实话现在是很不错的大菠萝肉鸽，只是美术的问题和敌人单一的问题，在大菠萝类里很常见了。 只能说技能树带肉鸽方向是对的。作者是真爱。 还是[u][b] 详细说一下这个技能树系统 [/b][/u]，你能换技能点是什么和更改分叉，还能用固定技能的珠子去重新连接分叉，也就是能改点的路径。这个是大菠萝肉鸽非常正确的设计。 除了原来的技能树重置，现在有个模式死了能续命，技能树不会重置。 如果你喜欢大菠萝刷宝刷宝石，密密麻麻的技能树，又缺个小型游戏调剂碎片时间的时候，买这个很不错。 机翻和优化问题需要心理预期平衡一下，小作坊没办法。 ---以下是旧22年测评 没有刷的成分, 每次肉鸽重置科技树, 要研究科技树怎么点倒是不常见. 可能对一些设计上思路有帮助, 但这实际上是肉鸽所有了 礼貌性好评, 不推荐购买. 5层以后其实还是有新boss的, 但是确实没啥意思. 大概3小时的游戏量.

In comparison to DoT which does a rocksolid 3.3dps â 10DMG/3sec which doesn't scale off anything like?????? -Artstyle is cool and u can tell that alot of time has been spent on it, the game is not bad by any accounts it's just an Absurd unnecessary early experience when you get manhandled by RNG and have to pivot into suboptimal zDPS builds in 1 save while absolutely destroying the game on another save if you get the correct Unlocks early on. The game has some issues, which I assume happen because it's being developed by just two people. I tried playing with a controller, but it seems the game wasn't designed for it yet—this part still feels like early access. Switching to mouse + keyboard made the controls feel much more natural. At first, the visuals and the way the character and enemy mobs move and attack felt quite strange, and I even thought they looked unpolished. But over time, the rest of the game made those issues barely noticeable. The game crashed twice in 8 hours, but I didn’t lose any progress, which is amazing. Despite these problems, I was ready to refund the game before hitting the 2-hour mark. Yet, I ended up playing for 8 hours straight—so yes, I absolutely recommend it. In fact, I plan to sink many more hours into it!

I wanted to like the game and I did, for a few hours, but now it just feels like watching paint dry, slow and boring. A lot of good ideas, most taken from the POE universe, and I had hoped it would be a light version of POE but, at least for me, if fails at too many things Skill tree : A fun idea with a so called infinite skill tree, and it can be fun to play around with. However it quickly becomes very annoying. You can't really plan a build in advance, and many times you have to use worthless nodes ( level ups ) in order to get to the nodes you want. Need energy and skills for range, well too bad, RNG just gave you nodes only related to endurance and melee skills, so you have to waste you points. Yes you can use shards to change some nodes but it's almost impossible not to waste some points which you don't want to do. Why are there traps everywhere. Every map, every single map, every single event...traps. Some are hard to see, some destroys you while you try to pick up and compare an item ( why does the game not pause when you compare two items ), and some shows up in places where you already have almost no room to navigate and avoid the enemies, I hate traps. Loot: Sure you get some loot, but you can't keep it between tuns and you can only hold 2 melee and 2 ranged at a time, and a few trinkets, so it quickly becomes dull and boring. At the same time trinkets are random, so it takes forever to get a good trinket with a bonus you can use, and have the relevant useful trinkets in order to get that bonus. The POE events are very very basic versions and they become more of a hassle than fun. Difficult levels spike quite hard. You will quickly face maps with modifiers that takes 3-5 life per hit meaning you will get 1-2 shot very easy ( or hit by a bloody trap ), and life is very hard to come by. Performance issues, slow and boring game play, hard to build planning ( which for me is essential in games like this ), very limited loot and end game progression, that's a no go for me. I do hope for some improvement to the game, as I really would like to play more of it in the future, but for now I will go back and watch paint dry.

The games a ton of fun, but this feels far from a 1.0. I've gotten multiple characters past 100, and when you start scaling more on-hit and AOE abilities you start to run into crash issues. I'm probably going to continue to play the game here and there but it needs A LOT of work. The maps get tedious and the in-map activities can be too risky at higher levels, especially considering each hit can do more than 15 damage. DO NOT go down that ladder, I promise you, will lose your character at higher levels. Its one of the only instances that actually trap you into the fight. not to mention the lives don't reset when you hit the end map boss, making it very risky to die during maps. Some of the Awaken bosses can be crazy tough, even more so if your build has screen clutter. Main complaint: CRASHES, Fix the crashes when going into your skill tree mid map, or randomly going from one instance to another.

Even though I kinda like this game, I find it deeply flawed. And to add insult to injury, I just lost all my saves! Don't get me wrong, there's fun to be had, and the developer is very active. But, it gets rather repetitive after a while. [*][b]Traps:[/b] Incredibly annoying, too many, and do not affect the enemies at all. [*][b]Boss fights:[/b] They constantly spam AoE that can easily cover most of the arena. [*][b]Skill tree:[/b] Too random, and you can't experiment due to cost. [*][b]Healing:[/b] Hearts are the only way to heal, and there are no passive skills for regeneration. [*][b]Challenges:[/b] Absurdly difficult at times. Just don't do them, they are not worth the risk. [*][b]Hardcore mode:[/b] What's the point of taking more risk if there's no extra reward? [*][b]Legacy:[/b] The permanent gains are abysmal. There's a skill tree, but it's very difficult to level up. [*][b]Balance:[/b] It's just not there. The more I level up, the weaker I feel. [*][b]Typos:[/b] Too many, especially for weapon names.

This game shows genuine promise — the core concept is intriguing and the initial hours deliver an enjoyable experience. Unfortunately, that momentum doesn't last. After roughly three to four hours, the content comes to an abrupt halt, leaving players with little to show for their continued time investment. The game world feels underdeveloped, with only three NPCs populating the main town and a few empty buildings that give the impression of an unfinished product — something you'd expect from an early access title, which this is not. The endgame, such as it is, borrows a map-based progression system reminiscent of Path of Exile, but lacks the variety that makes that model compelling. Enemies, items, and skill nodes repeat with little meaningful variation, making extended play sessions feel monotonous. Itemization is another area that falls short. Outside of two weapon slots with a swap feature and four trinket slots, there simply isn't enough gear diversity to drive the kind of rewarding loot loop that this genre depends on. At a budget price point, these shortcomings might be forgivable. But at its current asking price — even discounted — the game doesn't offer enough content or depth to justify the cost. The foundation is there, but it needs significant additional development before it can be recommended at full value.
